title: SkillsBench
researchQuestion: How do agent Skills affect task resolution and efficiency across tasks, models, and harnesses?
method: Paired benchmark conditions with and without Skills across a curated task set and repeated trials.
testedEnvironment: Published benchmark dataset and multiple agent/model configurations; exact release details remain in the source.
mainFindings: Skill effects vary by task and model.
A Skill can help, have little effect, or hurt a task.
Paired baselines are needed to measure uplift.
limitations: Benchmark results are not Packsmith normative requirements.
Results depend on the evaluated harness, model, and task corpus.
packsmithImplication: Keep outcome uplift evaluation as a future paired experiment; do not turn benchmark findings into doctor errors.

title: How Well Do Agentic Skills Work in the Wild
researchQuestion: What happens when agents must retrieve and select Skills in realistic settings?
method: Benchmark realistic retrieval and selection settings over a large Skill collection, with refinement experiments.
testedEnvironment: Published paper experiments across multiple models and agent tasks.
mainFindings: Benefits degrade as retrieval and selection become realistic.
Skill quality and relevance influence utility.
Refinement can recover some lost performance.
limitations: Packsmith does not implement the paper's optimizer or benchmark harness.
packsmithImplication: Treat discovery, selection, and activation as separate measurable reliability stages.

title: SkillOpt
researchQuestion: Can validation-gated optimization improve Skill instructions while preserving held-out behavior?
method: Optimization loop with evaluation gates and held-out checks.
testedEnvironment: Published SkillOpt experiments; exact model/task matrix is source-scoped.
mainFindings: Changes need validation gates and held-out evaluation.
Rejected edits should not replace a known-good artifact.
limitations: Packsmith v0.2 does not implement automatic optimization.
Implementation-specific methodology is not a standard.
packsmithImplication: Use atomic baseline publication and regression comparison as a future-compatible boundary.

title: Agent Skills ecosystem survey
researchQuestion: Which structural, behavioral, and contamination issues appear across Skill ecosystems?
method: Survey and analysis of a large Skill corpus with structural and behavioral quality dimensions.
testedEnvironment: Published ecosystem corpus and analysis methodology.
mainFindings: Structural validity does not guarantee behavioral quality.
Context contamination and ambiguous scope are practical risks.
limitations: Survey evidence is observational and non-normative.
The corpus and methodology may evolve.
packsmithImplication: Keep security, context, and activation checks bounded and evidence-linked.

title: Vercel AGENTS.md versus Skills experiment
researchQuestion: How did direct AGENTS.md context compare with Skill activation in one evaluated Next.js setting?
method: Context-specific agent evaluation comparing a compact AGENTS.md index with Skill-based instructions.
mainFindings: Direct context performed better in that experiment.
Skill activation adds an additional selection decision point.
limitations: One vendor experiment is not universal evidence.
It does not establish that AGENTS.md is always superior.
packsmithImplication: Use negative and near-miss trigger cases to measure activation bottlenecks without changing the product standard.
